mainTopic: How רבי combines the views of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה to rule on an עירוב placed in a basket hanging on a tree, and the source for רבי יהודה's requirement that an עירוב rest on a place four טפחים wide.
overview: The גמרא explains רבי's ruling about an עירוב placed in a basket hanging from a tree. רבי combines two ideas. From רבי מאיר he takes חוקקין להשלים, so the basket counts toward widening the tree to four טפחים. From רבי יהודה he takes the rule that an עירוב must rest on a place four טפחים wide. The source for רבי יהודה is a ברייתא about a beam in רשות הרבים. The גמרא re-reads that ברייתא: only a beam ten טפחים high needs a top four wide, while a lower beam is part of רשות הרבים and needs no width. The גמרא then asks whether this basket explanation clashes with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who treats a basket on a reed as a private domain. It answers that the basket's walls surround the reed but do not surround the tree. רבי ירמיה offers a different explanation: a basket can be tilted down to within ten טפחים. Finally, רב בר שבא challenges רב פפא's teaching from a משנה about one עירוב for יום טוב followed by שבת, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי follows two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי's ruling combines the opinion of רבי מאיר with the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds like רבי מאיר, and he also holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the basis of רבי's ruling about the basket on the tree: he relies on two different תנאים at once. This line sets up the next two steps, which spell out what he takes from each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not invent a new idea. He combines one rule from רבי מאיר with one rule from רבי יהודה. Each rule covers a different part of the case, and together they produce his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
He holds like (follows the opinion of)
A major תנא whose view is cited here
A major תנא (רבי יהודה בר אילעאי) whose view is cited here

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names. 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא. 'רבי יהודה' is a different, earlier תנא. In this step, רבי is following רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi holds like Rabbi Meir,
and he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of רבי's ruling from the earlier part of the סוגיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's ruling rests on two combined premises: one from רבי מאיר and one from רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The רבי מאיר piece: imagine the surface widened
steps.stepSummary: From רבי מאיר, רבי takes the principle of חוקקין להשלים: we view a narrow surface as if it were widened to four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר, who said that we 'carve out' to complete it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half: רבי uses רבי מאיר's principle that a narrow space can be treated as if it were filled out to the needed size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says this about an arched gateway that is too narrow at the top. We view the arch as if it were carved out to four טפחים. In our case, the hanging basket likewise counts toward making the tree four טפחים wide.

keyTerms.meaning: We carve out (we view the space as if it were carved or widened)
To complete (to reach the required size)
Who said

steps.whyThisMatters: חוקקין להשלים lets something that is physically too small be treated as legally full-sized. Here it is the reason the basket helps the tree count as four טפחים wide.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Meir,
who said: we carve out to complete.
phrases.notes: Originally said about a narrow arched gateway.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר חוֹקְקִין לְהַשְׁלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two premises named in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוקקין להשלים: a narrow surface is treated as though it were widened to the required four טפחים.

steps.title: The רבי יהודה piece: the עירוב needs a four-טפח base
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יהודה, רבי takes the rule that an עירוב must rest on a place four טפחים wide, and here no such place exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he holds like רבי יהודה, who said: we need the עירוב to be on a place of four טפחים, and here there isn't one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half: רבי יהודה requires the עירוב itself to sit on a four-טפח spot, and the tree on its own is not that wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basket counts toward the tree's legal width, as in step 2. But the עירוב still is not resting on an actual surface four טפחים wide. Combining both premises gives רבי's ruling in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: We require
The food placed to establish a new Shabbos base (here, עירוב תחומין)
On top of
A place four by four טפחים
And there is not (such a place)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי combines two tools. רבי מאיר's חוקקין להשלים makes the basket count toward the tree's width. רבי יהודה's rule requires the עירוב to rest on a real four-טפח place, which is missing here.

phrases.english: And he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: we require the eiruv
to be on top of a place of four handbreadths,
and there isn't one here.
phrases.notes: Without counting the basket, the tree is not four wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר בָּעִינַן עֵירוּב עַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second of the two premises named in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב must rest on a place four טפחים wide; in this case there is none.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's rule that an עירוב needs a four-טפח base.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'רבי יהודה' that was referred to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask where רבי יהודה actually said this rule. This sets up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 quoted רבי יהודה's view without a source. Before relying on it, the גמרא wants to show where he taught it. This is a request for information, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asking for clarification or a source)

phrases.english: What is the Rabbi Yehuda being referred to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבי יהודה opinion cited in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual source for רבי יהודה's requirement of a four-טפח place for an עירוב.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the beam in רשות הרבים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא: if someone sticks a beam into the ground in רשות הרבים and places his עירוב on it, the עירוב is valid only if the beam is ten טפחים high and four wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: if someone stuck a beam into the ground in רשות הרבים and put his עירוב on it, then if it is ten טפחים high and four wide, his עירוב is valid. If not, his עירוב is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting the ברייתא in which רבי יהודה requires a top surface four טפחים wide for an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam ten high and four wide is a רשות היחיד standing in the public domain. At face value, רבי יהודה says the עירוב placed on it is valid only with both measurements. The next step challenges this reading, and step 7 explains that the four-wide rule applies only when the beam is ten high. That is still the four-טפח premise used in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
He stuck (into the ground)
A beam
The public domain
Ten טפחים high
And if not

steps.whatToRemember: The source for רבי יהודה is the beam ברייתא. Read at face value, it says the עירוב works only on a beam ten high and four wide. Steps 6 and 7 reject that reading: the four-wide requirement applies only when the beam is ten high.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the proof text for the רבי יהודה premise that drives רבי's ruling about the basket on the tree.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If one stuck a beam into the ground in the public domain
and placed his eiruv on it,
if it is ten handbreadths high and four wide,
phrases.notes: These measurements make it a private domain.

phrases.english: his eiruv is a valid eiruv;
and if not, his eiruv is not a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by citing the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא of the beam in רשות הרבים: an עירוב on it is valid only if the beam is ten טפחים high and four wide.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא, רבי יהודה on a beam stuck in רשות הרבים

steps.title: Why would a short beam invalidate the עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to reading the ברייתא as saying that a beam less than ten טפחים high makes the עירוב invalid. On a short beam the person and his עירוב are both in רשות הרבים, so the עירוב should be fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! He and his עירוב are in the same place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks a reading of the ברייתא from step 5. If the beam is not ten טפחים high, the עירוב should certainly work, because it sits in the same domain as the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say the עירוב works only if the beam is ten high and four wide. That implies a shorter beam fails. But a beam under ten טפחים is just part of רשות הרבים, the same domain where the person stands, so he could easily reach his עירוב. So the 'ten high' condition cannot be a requirement for validity.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary — the opposite should be true
He and his עירוב are in the same domain, so the עירוב is reachable and valid

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a short beam is a problem. It is saying the reverse: a short beam is the easy case, so the ברייתא cannot mean that height is a requirement.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
phrases.notes: Signals that the implied ruling is backwards.

phrases.english: he and his eiruv are in the same place!
phrases.notes: Both are in רשות הרבים when the beam is below ten טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implied reading of the ברייתא cited in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the ברייתא that a beam under ten טפחים invalidates the עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Below ten טפחים the beam is part of רשות הרבים. The person is also in רשות הרבים, so he can reach his עירוב and it should be valid.

steps.title: Re-reading the ברייתא: four wide is needed only when the beam is ten high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the ברייתא. If the beam is ten טפחים high, its top must be four wide. If it is lower, no width is needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: if the beam is ten high, its top must be four wide. If it is not ten high, its top does not need to be four wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really meant. Height is not a requirement for validity. Height decides whether the four-wide rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam ten high has its own status, so its top must be four wide to hold the עירוב, matching רבי יהודה's rule from step 3. A beam under ten is simply part of רשות הרבים, where the person already is, so its width does not matter. This keeps the ברייתא as the source for רבי יהודה's four-טפח rule while removing the problem raised in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means — a re-reading of a source
Ten טפחים high — the height that separates an object from רשות הרבים
Its top is four טפחים wide

steps.whatToRemember: The four-טפח requirement applies only to a beam ten טפחים high. A lower beam is part of רשות הרבים and needs no minimum width.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
If it is ten high —
its top needs to be four wide,
if it is not ten high —
its top does not need to be four wide.
phrases.notes: A low beam counts as part of רשות הרבים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 6 by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a beam must be both ten high and four wide, or the עירוב is invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The four-wide requirement applies only when the beam is ten high. A lower beam needs no width because it is part of רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Whose view supports the earlier basket explanation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the earlier explanation of the hanging basket follows. It suggests that it does not fit רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this follow? Not the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the earlier explanation that a basket hanging on the tree completes the tree's width to four. It points out that this explanation seems to clash with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. This line sets up the source quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation treats the basket as completing four טפחים, yet still does not treat it as a private domain. The גמרא suspects that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה would disagree, since he lets a basket create a private domain. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? — asks which תנא a view follows
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה — a תנא

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the beam ברייתא back to the earlier basket explanation of רבי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא supports the explanation that a basket completing four טפחים still does not create a private domain.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: a basket on a reed makes a private domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that a basket placed on top of a reed in רשות הרבים forms a private domain, so throwing an object onto it creates liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: if someone stuck a reed into the ground in רשות הרבים and put a basket on top of it, then threw an object that landed on the basket, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for the claim in step 8. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה treats a basket on a reed as a private domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability means he moved something from רשות הרבים into a רשות היחיד. So for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a four-by-four basket raised ten טפחים high is enough to make a private domain. That seems to contradict the earlier explanation, where the basket on the tree did not make a private domain.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
He stuck a reed into the ground
A basket (here, four by four טפחים)
Liable — here for carrying into a רשות היחיד

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
If one stuck a reed in the public domain
and placed a basket on its top,
and threw an object and it landed on it —
he is liable!
phrases.notes: The basket counts as a private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the earlier basket explanation does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about a basket on top of a reed in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Surrounding walls versus non-surrounding walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The basket on a reed has walls that surround the reed on all sides, but a basket hanging from a tree does not surround the tree. So even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה could agree with the earlier explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. There, the walls surround. Here, the walls do not surround.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 9. It shows that the two cases differ, so there is no real contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the reed, the basket's sides surround the reed, so they can be viewed as walls reaching down to the ground and forming a private domain. A basket hanging on the side of a tree does not surround the tree, so its walls cannot do this. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling therefore does not apply to the tree case.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say — introduces a rejection of a proof
The walls surround (the reed on all sides)
There / here — contrasting two cases

steps.whatToRemember: A basket creates a private domain only if its walls surround the base. On a reed they do; hanging off a tree they do not.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
there — the partitions surround.
phrases.notes: The basket sits on the reed and encloses it.

phrases.english: Here — the partitions do not surround.
phrases.notes: The basket hangs off the tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the earlier basket explanation contradicts רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignores a key difference: on the reed the basket's walls surround the base, but on the tree they do not.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: a basket can be tilted down within ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains רבי's ruling in a new way. A basket is different because it can be tilted down to within ten טפחים of the ground, so the עירוב can be reached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: a basket is different, because one can tilt it and bring it within ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה offers a completely different explanation of the basket case, without relying on the earlier approach. A hanging basket can be tilted low, so the עירוב is reachable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the basket hangs above ten טפחים, the person can tip it until it is within ten. He can then take the עירוב without carrying from one domain to another. That is why the עירוב in a basket can be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
A basket (hanging from the tree)
To tilt it
To within ten טפחים of the ground

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second, independent explanation of רבי's ruling. It is based on whether the עירוב can be reached, not on widening the tree with חוקקין להשלים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
A basket is different,
since one can tilt it
and bring it to within ten handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the previous line of explanation and offers a new reason for רבי's ruling about the basket.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basket is different: since it can be tilted to within ten טפחים, the עירוב in it is reachable and valid.

steps.title: רב פפא teaches the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the scene: רב פפא was sitting and teaching this הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא sat and was saying this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that רב פפא was teaching the הלכה just discussed, so that it can bring a challenge to it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. The line names who taught the הלכה, so we know whose teaching the next objection is aimed at.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat (usually while teaching in the study hall)
A teaching or halacha that was passed on

phrases.english: Rav Pappa sat
and was saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: "This teaching" points back to the הלכה discussed in the previous steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא וְקָא אָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces רב פפא as a teacher of the הלכה from the previous discussion. This sets up the objection that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new ruling. The line only reports that רב פפא taught the הלכה already discussed.

steps.title: An objection from the case of a festival next to Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: רב בר שבא challenges רב פפא from a משנה. On the first day, a person stays with his עירוב until dark and then takes it away. On the second day, he stays with it until dark and then eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב בר שבא raised an objection to רב פפא from a משנה. How does a person make one עירוב work for two holy days in a row? On the first day, he brings the food to the spot and stays there with it until it gets dark. Then he picks it up and goes home. On the second day, he brings it back, stays with it until dark, and then he may eat it and go home.
steps.whatsHappening: רב בר שבא quotes a משנה as a challenge to רב פפא's teaching. The משנה describes a person who carries his עירוב away right after dark on the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the עירוב only needs to be in place at the moment the holy day begins. After that, the person can take it away or even eat it. This is used to press on רב פפא's teaching. The full force of the challenge and the answer come in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from an earlier source (a משנה or ברייתא)
How does he do it? (the משנה's opening question)
He brings it (the עירוב food) to the chosen spot
He stays with it until it gets dark
He takes it (picks it up and carries it away)

steps.confusionAlert: "First" and "second" mean two holy days in a row, such as יום טוב on Friday followed by שבת. The person takes the food home after the first day so it is not lost before the second day begins. On the second day nothing is left to protect it for, so he may eat it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The משנה shows a basic rule of עירוב. The עירוב sets a person's place at the moment the holy day begins, at dark. What happens to the food after that does not matter.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב בַּר שַׁבָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav bar Shabba raised an objection to Rav Pappa:
How does he do it?
phrases.notes: The case: a festival falls on Friday, and the person wants one עירוב for both days.

phrases.english: He brings it there on the first day
phrases.notes: Meaning the day before the first holy day begins.

phrases.english: and stays with it until it gets dark,
phrases.notes: At dark, the עירוב sets that spot as his "home" for the day.

phrases.english: and then he takes it and goes on his way.
phrases.notes: He takes it so it won't get lost before the second day.

phrases.english: On the second day, he stays with it until dark
phrases.notes: He brings it back to the same spot on Friday afternoon.

phrases.english: and then eats it and goes on his way.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (a source quoted whose implication will be drawn next)
steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב בַּר שַׁבָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a challenge, from a משנה, against the teaching that רב פפא was just said to be teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's teaching, which continues the earlier discussion of an עירוב placed where it can still be reached.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a person carry his עירוב away right after dark. This suggests that the עירוב only needs to be valid at the moment the holy day begins. That idea is used to challenge רב פפא's teaching. The exact point of conflict is spelled out in the continuation of the גמרא.
